text:
Engineering leads meeting, notes.

Reliability. Three services carried the whole error budget this month. Checkout burned sixty percent of its budget on the one bad config push. Search burned forty percent, spread across the week, and nobody has looked at why. Notifications burned everything it had and is still over.

The pattern Ravi pointed out is that we treat the budget as a report rather than as something that changes what we do, and none of the three teams changed a plan because of it.

Hiring. The two open backend roles have been open since April. We have seen fourteen candidates and made one offer, which was declined on money.

Marcus is going to ask for the band to be reviewed rather than keep running the same loop. He wants an answer before the next planning round, since holding the roles open is what is stopping the notifications work from being staffed.
note: Long minutes that carry both a heading pair and three service records sharing the same two fields.

text: The one thing we did not answer in the review is who signs off the data retention change now that the privacy lead has left.
note: A single unanswered question, which is one sentence and stays one sentence.

text: Three teams flagged the same thing in the planning meeting. Support flagged that the release notes arrive after the release. Sales flagged that the release notes arrive after the demo they promised it in. Docs flagged that nobody tells them a release is happening at all.

text: Retro actions, three of them. Write the release notes before the release — not the day after. Give docs a heads up when a branch is cut. Put the demo date in the release ticket so sales stop asking. Dana will do the first one this week.

text: Renewal call. They came in asking for a twelve percent uplift and we came out at four, which is roughly where we expected to land, and the two year term they wanted is now a one year term with a right to renew at the same rate.

text: Agreed order for the maintenance window on Saturday. First we put the site into read only mode and post on the status page. Then we take the snapshot and confirm it restores somewhere else before we touch anything. After that we run the schema change, which we timed at eleven minutes on the copy. Finally we take the site out of read only and watch the error rate for an hour before anyone goes to bed.

text:
Migration go no go, notes for the people who could not make it.

Readiness. The dual write has been running for nine days with no drift reported by the reconciliation job. The one mismatch we saw in week one was the trailing whitespace in the name field, and that is fixed.

The rollback path has been rehearsed once, on staging, and took twenty minutes. Nobody has rehearsed it against production sized data, which Ravi is uncomfortable with and said so.

Open items. Three things are still open. The read only window needs sign off from support because it lands in their busiest hour. The DNS time to live has to come down to sixty seconds a day before the cutover. And nobody has confirmed whether the reporting warehouse reads from the primary or the replica.

The date holds for now. We cut over on the seventh unless the rollback rehearsal against production data fails, and if it does we take the whole thing to the next planning meeting rather than trying again that week.
